items.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: In fact you and Stan Kenton and a couple of other people really were on the ground floor of jazz education.

ctx.x: Yeah. Stan Kenton was the head of it. It was really thought of and run by Ken Morris. But Stan Kenton was the head of the camp then. They were wonderful camps. They were really a beginning. Ken Morris was a ballroom operator. And he talked to Buddy Morrow and asked him, he said, “You know I see this disappearing and I’m making money off rock groups now, and I’d like to see what I could do with it.” And he says, “Why don’t you start a summer camp for high school students?” And he thought that was a good idea and…
When you grew up you were into classical technique first?
